data.content_ref: inline:The target asserts that a large service can enforce software and organizational diversity via central authority, but it provides no causal mechanism connecting enforced diversity to actual reduction in correlated failures. It merely asserts that diversity 'by design' prevents monoculture collapse without showing why diverse implementations under one organizational roof would fail independently rather than sharing common-mode dependencies (e.g., shared operational procedures, deployment schedules, security policies, upstream vendors). The counterconditions even concede that a large service can collapse into monoculture when it prioritizes efficiency, which directly undermines the causal claim that central authority is what guarantees diversity. The argument thus assumes the very thing it must causally establish: that central authority's enforcement of diversity translates into genuine statistical independence of failures rather than merely superficial heterogeneity masking the same shared cause.
